The edit is clean — `cowlMat`/`inletMat` are declared and used consistently, no dangling references, and nothing outside the engine block changed. Still a single self-contained module using only allowed `THREE` primitives (no imports, loaders, data URIs, or DOM).

---

**What I changed and why (iter 10):**

I inspected views 1, 3, 5, 8 and the contact sheet myself, plus the `side.png` and `planform.png` references. Both judge tracks converge on the same defect (the highest-weighted criterion, engines_four_underwing, weight 1.5): "clustered at the wing root," "only two visible," "sits ON the wing not underslung," "no pylon detail," "needs forward offset ahead of the LE." View 8 showed it plainly — the nacelles were short stubs bunched at the wing root, merging into the landing-gear clump with no visible pylon.

I rebuilt only the four-engine block (nacelle, inlet, exhaust, pylon):

- **Longer nacelles** (6.5 vs 5.6) with a fan-cowl bulge (front r1.55 → aft r1.3) so each reads as a real engine rather than a stub.
- **Pushed forward** — center moved to `le + 1.6`, so ~4.85 of the barrel now juts clearly *ahead* of the wing leading edge (only ~1.65 aft), matching the planform/side refs and pulling the nacelles out of the gear clump.
- **Hung lower** — `nacY = under − 2.35` (was −1.9) so the nacelles hang clearly below the wing/belly instead of hiding in the fuselage silhouette; combined with the wing dihedral this staggers the inboard pair low-and-forward vs the outboard high-and-aft, so all four separate in side view instead of merging into one lump.
- **Open darker inlet** — replaced the thin flat disc with a recessed dark funnel (mouth r1.32 narrowing inward to r0.7) set just proud of the cowl front, leaving a bright cowl lip ring → reads as an open intake.
